title: Global oil price shock
body: Supply cuts and a regional crisis have sent crude prices sharply higher. Every importing economy is feeling it, and fuel prices at home are climbing.

choices.label: Release strategic reserves
choices.description: Costs ₹2,500 crore; softens the price rise for a few months.
choices.outcome: Reserves are released to the market. Pump prices rise more slowly than elsewhere.

choices.label: Subsidise fuel prices
choices.description: Costs ₹4,000 crore; keeps pump prices steady and voters content.
choices.outcome: The treasury absorbs the shock. Households barely notice, though the bill is large.

choices.label: Let the market adjust
choices.description: No cost, but inflation and growth take the full hit.
choices.outcome: Prices climb and household budgets are squeezed for most of a year.

title: Global recession
body: Major economies are contracting together. Export orders are drying up and capital is leaving emerging markets.

choices.label: Launch a stimulus package
choices.description: Costs ₹6,000 crore; cushions jobs and growth.
choices.outcome: Public works and credit support soften the blow. Growth dips, but less than elsewhere.

choices.label: Hold the line on spending
choices.description: No cost, but jobs and growth suffer.
choices.outcome: The budget stays disciplined while exports fall. Unemployment drifts up.

title: New disease spreads across borders
body: A fast-moving respiratory illness has reached several continents. Airlines are cancelling routes and the first cases have been reported in India.

choices.label: Nationwide restrictions
choices.description: Costs ₹3,000 crore; strong containment, heavy on the economy.
choices.outcome: Movement is restricted for weeks. The disease is contained early, at a cost to jobs and output.

choices.label: Targeted measures and testing
choices.description: Costs ₹1,500 crore; relies on a well-run health ministry.
choices.outcome: Testing, tracing and local restrictions slow the spread without closing the economy.

choices.label: Advisories only
choices.description: No cost, but the outbreak spreads and public confidence falls.
choices.outcome: The government urges caution and little else. Hospitals fill up and voters notice.

title: Fighting breaks out near {country}
body: A dispute between neighbouring states in the region of {country} has turned violent. Shipping insurers are raising premiums and capitals are calling for restraint.

choices.label: Offer to mediate
choices.description: Costs ₹300 crore; raises India’s standing as an honest broker.
choices.outcome: Envoys shuttle between the capitals. Talks do not end the fighting, but India’s offer is noticed.

choices.label: Stay neutral
choices.description: No cost; India stays out of it.
choices.outcome: India calls for restraint and keeps its distance.

choices.label: Sell equipment to both sides
choices.description: Brings in ₹1,500 crore, but costs India some standing.
choices.outcome: Defence exporters fill orders. Critics say India is profiting from the conflict.

title: Commodity prices surge
body: Strong demand abroad has lifted prices for farm produce and energy. Exporters across the world are enjoying a windfall, India’s farmers among them.

title: Global technology investment boom
body: Investors are pouring money into software, chips and clean energy. Indian technology firms are winning contracts and attracting capital.

title: World food prices spike
body: Poor harvests in several exporting countries have pushed grain and edible oil prices up worldwide. Households at home are paying more at the market.

choices.label: Restrict food exports
choices.description: Protects prices at home but upsets trading partners.
choices.outcome: Export curbs keep grain at home. Importing countries protest.

choices.label: Open imports and release stocks
choices.description: Costs ₹1,500 crore; eases prices without hurting partners.
choices.outcome: Stocks are released and duties on imports are cut. Prices ease slowly.

choices.label: Do nothing
choices.description: No cost, but inflation rises.
choices.outcome: Food prices rise through the season.

title: Turmoil in global financial markets
body: A banking scare abroad has sent investors fleeing to safety. The rupee is under pressure and foreign money is leaving Indian markets.

choices.label: Arrange swap lines with friendly central banks
choices.description: Costs ₹2,000 crore; calms markets quickly.
choices.outcome: Partner central banks stand behind the rupee. The panic passes.

choices.label: Ride it out
choices.description: No cost, but growth and inflation take a hit.
choices.outcome: The rupee slides and imports get dearer before markets settle.

title: Shipping lanes disrupted
body: Blocked straits and rerouted vessels are lengthening delivery times and raising freight costs. Ports report fewer arrivals and customs receipts are falling.

title: Climate summit: {country} presses for commitments
body: Leaders are gathering to agree new targets for cutting emissions. {country} is lobbying hard for developing economies to take on binding goals.

choices.label: Commit to ambitious targets
choices.description: Costs some growth, wins goodwill abroad.
choices.outcome: India signs up to demanding targets. Partners applaud; industry grumbles about costs.

choices.label: Offer modest, conditional targets
choices.description: A balanced position.
choices.outcome: India agrees to targets tied to finance and technology from richer countries.

choices.label: Decline new commitments
choices.description: Protects industry; costs India some standing.
choices.outcome: India says development comes first. Several capitals are disappointed.

title: {country} invites the President to a summit
body: {country} has invited the President to a bilateral summit on trade and security. A visit would be a chance to deepen the relationship.

choices.label: Attend and open an embassy
choices.description: Costs ₹400 crore; a lasting presence in the capital.
choices.outcome: The summit goes well. An embassy opens soon after, and the two governments agree to meet regularly.

choices.label: Send the foreign minister
choices.description: A polite compromise.
choices.outcome: The foreign minister attends in the President’s place. The host is satisfied.

choices.label: Decline the invitation
choices.description: Saves time and money; the host is disappointed.
choices.outcome: The invitation is politely declined. The host notes it.

title: Trade dispute with {country}
body: {country} has raised duties on Indian goods, saying India’s own tariffs are unfair. Exporters want the government to act.

choices.label: Open talks
choices.description: Costs ₹300 crore in negotiating effort; a deal is likely.
choices.outcome: Negotiators agree a package. Duties come down and relations improve.

choices.label: Retaliate with tariffs
choices.description: Tougher on the surface, but relations suffer.
choices.outcome: India matches the duties. Both sides lose trade; domestic producers are pleased.

choices.label: Wait and see
choices.description: No cost, but exporters lose business.
choices.outcome: Exporters absorb the higher duties for months.

title: {country} proposes border talks
body: With tension along the frontier, {country} has proposed a round of talks between officials to reduce incidents and agree patrol rules.

choices.label: Accept the talks
choices.description: Costs ₹200 crore; lowers tension.
choices.outcome: Officials meet and agree practical measures. Tension eases.

choices.label: Decline for now
choices.description: No cost; tension stays.
choices.outcome: India says conditions are not right for talks. The frontier stays tense.

title: {country} expels an Indian diplomat
body: {country} has declared an Indian diplomat unwelcome and given them 48 hours to leave, citing activities incompatible with their status. India denies the charge.

choices.label: Protest quietly
choices.description: Keeps the channel open.
choices.outcome: India lodges a formal protest through diplomatic channels and leaves it there.

choices.label: Expel one of theirs
choices.description: Plays well at home; relations sour further.
choices.outcome: India expels a diplomat in return. Both capitals harden their positions.

choices.label: Ask a friendly capital to mediate
choices.description: Costs ₹200 crore; calms things down.
choices.outcome: A third country brings both sides together. The expulsions are quietly dropped.

title: {country} asks India to join sanctions
body: {country} is building a coalition to sanction a third state and wants India to join. Doing so would please {country} but cost India trade.

choices.label: Join the sanctions
choices.description: Wins favour with {country}; costs some customs revenue.
choices.outcome: India joins the measures. {country} is grateful; trade with the target state falls.

choices.label: Decline to take sides
choices.description: Keeps trade flowing.
choices.outcome: India says it does not recognise measures outside the UN. {country} is unhappy.

choices.label: Offer to mediate instead
choices.description: Costs ₹250 crore.
choices.outcome: India offers its good offices. Neither side takes it up, but the offer is noted.

title: {country} wants to buy Indian defence equipment
body: {country} is interested in an order for India’s defence industry, including training and spares. It would bring revenue and deepen ties.

choices.label: Accept the order
choices.description: Brings in ₹3,000 crore.
choices.outcome: The contract is signed. Industry is pleased and the partnership grows.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.description: No effect on the budget.
choices.outcome: India declines. The offer lapses without ill feeling.

title: Displaced people arrive from {country}
body: Fighting and hardship in {country} are pushing thousands across the border. Local officials say shelters are filling and ask for guidance.

choices.label: Open relief camps
choices.description: Costs ₹1,500 crore; wins respect abroad.
choices.outcome: Camps open with help from aid agencies. The response is widely praised.

choices.label: Tighten the border
choices.description: Cheaper, but relations and reputation suffer.
choices.outcome: Border posts are reinforced. Neighbours criticise the decision.

title: {country} asks India for development aid
body: {country} has asked India for help with a food shortage and failing infrastructure. A package would be a visible act of friendship.

choices.label: Send a package
choices.description: Costs ₹800 crore; relations and reputation improve.
choices.outcome: Supplies and engineers are on their way. {country} is deeply grateful.

choices.label: Decline for now
choices.description: No cost; the request is noted.
choices.outcome: India explains that resources are stretched. The request lapses.

title: {country} proposes joint military exercises
body: Defence officials in {country} have proposed a joint exercise to improve interoperability and signal partnership.

choices.label: Join the exercise
choices.description: Costs ₹600 crore; raises readiness and morale.
choices.outcome: Troops train alongside their counterparts. Both sides learn, and the partnership grows.

choices.label: Decline
choices.description: No cost.
choices.outcome: India declines. The host is mildly disappointed.

title: Naval vessels shadow each other near {country}
body: Patrol vessels of India and {country} have come dangerously close in disputed waters. Each side accuses the other of provocation.

choices.label: Lodge a firm protest
choices.description: No cost; tension rises a little.
choices.outcome: India protests and keeps patrolling. The incident passes.

choices.label: Propose joint patrols
choices.description: Costs ₹150 crore; lowers tension.
choices.outcome: A hotline and joint patrol rules are agreed. Tension falls.

choices.label: Show of force
choices.description: Costs ₹500 crore; the fleet sails in strength.
choices.outcome: The navy deploys in force. The message is clear, and so is the risk.

title: India is asked to host a world trade expo
body: The organisers of a major trade expo want India as host. Delegations from dozens of countries would visit, with the contracts and publicity that follow.

choices.label: Host the expo
choices.description: Costs ₹2,500 crore; boosts services, trade and standing.
choices.outcome: The expo draws large crowds and fat order books. India’s reputation as a host grows.

choices.label: Decline the offer
choices.description: No cost.
choices.outcome: Another country takes the expo.

title: Vote at the UN: {country} seeks India’s support
body: {country} has asked India to back its draft resolution at the General Assembly. Other delegations are lobbying the other way.

choices.label: Vote in favour
choices.description: Pleases {country}, may cool others.
choices.outcome: India votes for the resolution. {country} is pleased.

choices.label: Abstain
choices.description: Safe, but wins no friends.
choices.outcome: India abstains. No one is offended and no one is grateful.

choices.label: Vote against
choices.description: Annoys {country}; pleases its critics.
choices.outcome: India votes against. {country} notes it.
